title: Now Christ, the Very Son of God
description: Now Christ, the Very Son of God in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Nikolaus Selnecker wrote these words in German. Conrad Herman Louis Schuette's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 403.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now Christ, the ve-ry Son of God, On sin-ners sends an-oth-er flood; It is the wa-ter which the Lord Has com-pre-hend-ed in the Word.

lines: Now Christ, the very Son of God,
On sinners sends another flood;
It is the water which the Lord
Has comprehended in the Word.
This flood, to cleanse sin’s leprosy,
Mere earthly water cannot be;
But water and God’s gracious Word
Conjoined, this saving bath afford.
“Go ye,” says Christ, “My Word proclaim,
Baptize the nations in God’s name;
All who are baptized and believe
My full salvation shall receive.”
God, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
To be baptized invites the host;
He will be present, though unseen,
From all their sins to wash them clean.
So, too, by our repentance, must
The old man, with his sins and lust,
Be daily drowned and then arise
A new man, righteous, pure, and wise.
That by the water and the Word
We’re born again, we thank Thee, Lord.
In life and death Thine let us be
And Thine in all eternity.

licence: Public domain: Nikolaus Selnecker died in 1592; Conrad Herman Louis Schuette died in 1926.
credits: Words by Nikolaus Selnecker (1530–1592), translated by Conrad Herman Louis Schuette (1843–1926), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
